commits.edited_message:
parsedate: find day names, months and time zones faster

Implements faster lookups for which specific week name, month name and
time zone that is provided; without loops.

The single-letter time zone table skips the unused J entry instead of
keeping a dummy placeholder for it, so checktz() adjusts the index for
letters that sort after J.

With this applied, the dateparser perf test completes almost twice as
fast for me.

Add unit test 4781 to verify each parser.

Closes #22981

(cherry picked from commit e7f76c782b06ab6af9eb1f256a8d681d7fa13b7c)

parsedate: time zone strings

The two letter names are not used for lookup anymore so drop them. The
single-letter table becomes a plain offset array to use less memory,
keeping the compact A-Z-minus-J layout. The three and four letter
versions are now stored as uint32 to use less memory and get found
slightly faster.

Closes #23000

(cherry picked from commit f1956d23051657ebdc98e712f19e49eebdf506de)

diff --git a/lib/parsedate.c b/lib/parsedate.c
index 9630a98..b54548b 100644
--- a/lib/parsedate.c
+++ b/lib/parsedate.c
@@ -114,7 +114,8 @@ struct tzinfo {
 
 #define DST (-60)     /* offset for daylight savings time */
 
-/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Z */
+/* alpha-sorted list of single-letter time zones, A - Z. J is skipped since
+   it is not a timezone, so no slot is wasted on it. */
 static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -1 * 60,            /* Alpha */
   -2 * 60,            /* Bravo */
@@ -125,7 +126,6 @@ static const int16_t tzone[] = {
   -7 * 60,            /* Golf */
   -8 * 60,            /* Hotel */
   -9 * 60,            /* India */
-  -1,                 /* J - not a timezone */
   -10 * 60,           /* Kilo */
   -11 * 60,           /* Lima */
   -12 * 60,           /* Mike */

coupling: The out-of-bounds read only exists because of how the two commits compose; neither is wrong by itself. Commit 1 (parsedate: find day names...) changes the single-letter tzone[] table from 26 slots (A-Z, with a dummy placeholder for the unused letter J) to 25 slots (A-Z minus J), and correctly updates checktz()'s single-letter branch to subtract 1 from the index for every letter that sorts after J -- self-consistent and correct in isolation, verified by unit4781's exhaustive A-Z table. Commit 2 (parsedate: time zone strings) rewrites the same table as a flat int16_t[] to save memory and 'get found slightly faster', faithfully preserving the 25-entry, no-J-slot layout (dropping the dummy J entry is the natural reading of 'the single ... names are not used for lookup anymore'). But its rewritten checktz() reverts to the pre-commit-1 one-line formula 'tzone[first - "A"]' with no J adjustment -- a plausible simplification when storing bare offsets, and byte-for-byte what the real upstream commit already contains, so it does not read as a regression on its own. Fixing commit 2 alone (e.g. reverting just its checktz change) without noticing commit 1 shrank the table, or fixing commit 1 alone without seeing commit 2 drops its index adjustment, both leave the final tree vulnerable: the bug is the combination of 'array has 25 slots' (commit 1) with 'index formula assumes 26 slots' (commit 2). For check[0] == 'Z', tzone[first - 'A'] reads tzone[25], one element past the end of the 25-element global array.
